To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ozonation is an efficient process for the treatment of surface water and wastewaters.

wastewater derived organic matter is more resistant towards ozonation than natural organic matter and that the composition of the dissolved organic matter in the water body is a major factor for the formation of ozonization by-products.
wastewater impacted surface water may be characterized by higher formation of carbolyic compounds, but lower yield (μg carbonyl compounds/mg dissolved organic carbon) compared to pure surface water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ozonation pretreatments of surface and wastewater derived organic carbon on the formation of carbonyls and possible implications on drinking water treatment.
the impact of wastewater on the quality of surface water and the formation of by-products during ozonation treatment.
the impact of ozonation on different types of dissolved matter and possible implications on the formation yield of ozonation byproducts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of wastewaters in surface water results in increased formation of ozonation products but with lower formation yields.
the presence of wastewater derived organic compounds in river water could have an impact on the formation of disinfection by-products.
wastewater derived organic matter has a lower potential to form ozonation byproducts than natural organic matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ozonation of wastewater impacted river water may result in the formation of a variety of ozonation byproducts that are not present in ozonation of river water.

the presence of wastewater derived organic carbon in river water may lead to higher formation of ozonation disinfection by-products but at a lower concentration level than in the case of pure wastewater.
the formation yield of ozonation byproducts is lower in wastewaters than in surface water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ozonation pretreatment of surface water may have implications on the formation yield of carbonyl by-products and thus on the subsequent treatment processes.
ozonation of surface waters with different organic loadings and compositions may result in different types of ozonation byproducts.
ozonation of surface waters impacted by wastewaters may result in formation of higher amounts of carbonyls than the ozonation of pristine surface waters.
